name: init_project_memory
description: Initializes memory for a project and returns a briefing from related experience: similar projects, their decisions and lessons. Call it when starting work on a project that has no memory yet. Pass description — it is what finds the similar projects; pass seedFrom with existing project names (joined by '+') to preload their experience explicitly. Without projectName the server names the project after its working folder and refuses generic folders (src, projects, work, design). The answer's data says whether the memory was created, carries the briefing (similarProjects, experience, notes) and the project's pending link suggestions: confirm each with link_projects or reject it with dismiss_link.

projectName.description: Project name. Optional: when omitted, the server uses the name of the working folder the client was started in, refusing generic folders (src, projects, work, design).

description.description: Short description of what the project will be — it is embedded and finds similar projects. Optional.

seedFrom.description: Existing project names to preload experience from, joined by '+'. Optional.

name: list_projects
description: Lists the projects that have memory. Call it before guessing how a project was named.

prefix.description: Leading characters of the project name, case-insensitive. Empty — every project.

name: remember
description: Stores one record into long-term memory. Call it by itself whenever something worth keeping happens: a decision is made (kind 'decision'), a mistake is understood (kind 'lesson' — what happened, why, how to avoid), a stable fact changes (kind 'fact'), the user states a preference (kind 'preference'). The answer's data carries the new record's id. When the server refuses with type 'duplicate' — a very similar record exists, and it is the refusal's data — do not retry blindly: either supersede it (replaceId with its id) or store anyway (force: true). When an existing record turned out wrong or outdated, replace it with replaceId instead of adding a second opinion next to it. When the record itself reveals a relation to another project, pass links — the record and its edges land in one call; each link answers what was made or why not. A mentioned project with no edge yet comes back in pending: confirm it with link_projects or reject it with dismiss_link, do not ignore it.

projectName.description: Project name — the identifier the memory was created with. Case-insensitive.

content.description: The knowledge itself, in the language of the conversation.

kind.description: Record kind. Canonical: fact, decision, lesson, preference, reference, note, task, event; other tags are allowed. Empty on recall — every kind; empty on remember — 'note'.

title.description: Short label of the record. Optional.

replaceId.description: Id of the record this one supersedes; the old record is deleted. Optional.

force.description: Store even when a very similar record exists.

links.description: Graph edges to create together with the record — the atomic form of link_projects: each element links this record's project to its 'to' project. Optional.

to.description: Target project of the edge; the source is the record's project.

type.description: Edge type; directed from the record's project to 'to'.

note.description: What exactly connects them — one line. Optional.

name: recall
description: Searches memory by meaning. Call it before proposing an architecture, a stack or a fix — past decisions and lessons apply across projects, so leave projectName empty to search the whole memory (that is the default that transfers experience); set it to restore the context of one project. An empty query returns an overview of the newest records — use that to recover after a context reset. The answer's data lists the records with their ids, and a note when nothing was found. If a returned record is visibly wrong or outdated, fix the memory immediately: remember with replaceId, or forget. A project-scoped recall also lists the project's pending link suggestions until each is confirmed (link_projects) or rejected (dismiss_link); an unknown project is refused with type 'notFound'.

query.description: What to look for, in natural language. Empty — an overview of the newest records.

projectName.description: Project name — the identifier the memory was created with. Case-insensitive. Empty — the whole memory (transfers experience across projects).

kind.description: Record kind. Canonical: fact, decision, lesson, preference, reference, note, task, event; other tags are allowed. Empty on recall — every kind; empty on remember — 'note'.

name: forget
description: Deletes records by id (several ids comma-separated). Deletion is permanent; for bulk cleanups confirm the list with the user first — review_memory nominates candidates. A whole project goes with forget_project.

ids.description: Record id, or several ids comma-separated.

name: review_memory
description: Lists deletion candidates: durable records that recall has never returned and that grew old, plus tasks untouched for as long. Candidates are nominations, not decisions — confirm with the user, then forget the confirmed ids.

projectName.description: Project name — the identifier the memory was created with. Case-insensitive. Empty — the whole memory.

name: rename_project
description: Renames a project everywhere: the registry, every record, every graph edge. The old name stops existing.

name: forget_project
description: Forgets a whole project: every record, every graph edge touching it in either direction, its link suggestions (the dismissed ones too) and its registration. Permanent, so it takes two calls: without confirm it deletes nothing and answers the counts; show them to the user, and only once they agree call again with confirm: true. Only ever on the user's request — an outdated record is replaced or forgotten, never its project.

projectName.description: Project name — the identifier the memory was created with. Case-insensitive.

confirm.description: False — count what would be deleted and delete nothing. True — delete, after the user agreed to the counts.

name: link_projects
description: Creates or updates a directed, typed edge between two projects. Call it by itself the moment a dependency becomes visible: one project uses another, holds its design, documents it. Only directed facts belong here — 'these two are similar' is not stored, recall finds similarity by meaning. A confirmed edge also settles the pair's pending link suggestion.

from.description: Source project of the directed edge.

to.description: Target project of the directed edge.

type.description: Edge type: uses, depends_on, design_of, part_of, implements or documents; all types are directed, from source to target.

note.description: What exactly connects them — one line. Optional.

name: dismiss_link
description: Rejects a pending link suggestion: the pair stops being proposed, permanently. Use it when a mentioned project is not actually related; when the relation is real, confirm it with link_projects instead.

from.description: First project of the suggested pair.

to.description: Second project of the suggested pair.

name: unlink_projects
description: Removes edges between two projects regardless of direction. Empty type removes every edge between them.

type.description: Edge type. Empty — remove every edge between these projects.

name: sync_project_links
description: Syncs machine-extracted relations into the graph from any source of truth, not only code: a project manifest (csproj, package.json), an Obsidian vault's wiki-links, an XML registry. The caller parses the source and passes the relations; the server upserts them as auto edges (note 'auto: <source>'). Manual edges are never overwritten, an auto edge that disappeared from its source is only marked stale — never deleted — and a target with no memory is skipped and reported. Idempotent: the same payload twice changes nothing.

projectName.description: Project name — the identifier the memory was created with. Case-insensitive.

links.description: The relations extracted from the source, each directed from this project to its 'to'.

to.description: Target project of the edge; the source is the record's project.

type.description: Edge type; directed from the record's project to 'to'.

note.description: What exactly connects them — one line. Optional.

source.description: What was parsed to get them — csproj, package.json, obsidian, xml, … — stamped into the auto note.

name: get_graph
description: Answers the directed edges around the selected projects (from, type, to, note) without loading any records. Empty projectName answers the whole graph.

projectName.description: Project name, or several joined by '+'. Empty — the whole graph.

depth.description: How many edge hops to expand (1-5).
